title: security-readiness-scenarios-for-sales
content:
Purpose:
This working brief equips Sales and Solutions Engineering with short, medium, and long-form messaging for conversations about Redwood Inference security readiness: SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA, data handling practices, and audit-log language. Target: quick answers in calls, email snippets for procurement, and a small technical appendix to attach to RFPs.

Audience:
- Security/Compliance reviewers at mid-market & enterprise buyers
- Procurement and Legal teams
- Platform/Infra/SRE/ML engineering stakeholders evaluating inference providers

TL;DR (one-liners for intros):
- "Redwood Inference is a production-first inference platform that can be consumed as a hosted API, reserved (Dedicated) capacity, or a Private deployment — each with explicit controls for data isolation, encryption, and auditability."
- "We do not use customer prompt or output data to train models. Enterprisey customers can opt for Private deployments where no customer data leaves their network and Redwood only manages control-plane operations as agreed in the contract."

Elevator scripts (30–90s):
- For security reviewers: "Our security program centers on three tenancy options so you can pick the right trust model: Hosted for quick integration with contractual guarantees (SOC2 Type II + encryption in transit & at rest), Dedicated for isolated capacity with predictable performance and isolated logs, and Private for VPC/on‑prem where we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and audit pipeline. We also provide a detailed audit-log schema and can map it to your SIEM for retention and access controls."
- For procurement/legal: "Standard enterprise agreements include: SOC2 attestation (Type II), data processing addendum with clear retention and deletion commitments, option for HIPAA BAA where required, and contract language for audit evidence delivery (reports, diagrams, pen test summaries)."

Persona-specific snippets:
- Engineer evaluating latency/cost: "We support per-route tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console so your SREs can attribute latency/compute to routes and models. Audit logs include request metadata, model variant used, sequence lengths, and CPU/GPU allocation metadata for cost reconciliation."
- Security/compliance lead: "SOC2 scope covers our control plane and hosted API operations; Dedicated and Private models are covered by contractual controls. For HIPAA customers we offer Private deployments and a BAA — we can exclude PHI from logs and enable customer-managed keys."

Objection handling (short Q&A):
- Q: "We require SOC2 Type II and a recent report."
  A: "We maintain SOC2 Type II for our hosted control plane and can provide the most recent attestation under NDA. For Dedicated contracts we document equivalent operational controls in the customer contract and provide evidence packages on request."
- Q: "Can you prove you don’t train on our data?"
  A: "Yes. By default we do not use customer inputs/outputs to improve models. For hosted customers this is a contractual commitment; for Dedicated and Private customers no customer data leaves the tenant unless explicitly configured. We include these commitments in our DPA and customer onboarding checklist."
- Q: "What about HIPAA?"
  A: "We support HIPAA customers through Private deployments and a BAA. In hosted mode we can support HIPAA only after an architectural review and contractual agreement (BAA)."

Draft audit-log language (copy-ready clause for SOW / RFP attachment):
"Audit Log and Forensics: Redwood Inference will deliver structured audit logs for all inference requests routed through the customer tenancy. Each log entry contains a timestamp, tenant identifier, API route, model identifier and version, request/response size (token counts), request metadata (region, latency), and anonymized routing/worker IDs. Audit logs are encrypted at rest and in transit, retained per the customer's retention policy, and can be exported to the customer's SIEM via S3/Cloud Storage integration or direct syslog/streaming connectors. Redwood will exclude payload content from exported logs by default; payload-level logging is opt-in and must be enabled via the customer's compliance configuration."
Data handling summary (short, must-attach to RFPs):
- Data use: We do not train models on customer inputs or outputs unless explicitly agreed; this is stated in the DPA.
- Data segregation: Hosted = logical separation; Dedicated = hardware/tenant isolation; Private = customer-controlled network.
- Encryption: TLS for transit, AES-256 (or cloud provider equivalent) for rest. Keys: Redwood-managed KMS for hosted; customer-managed KMS/HSM for Dedicated (on request) and Private.
- Retention & deletion: Audit logs and short-term request caches retained by default 30 days; longer retention configurable up to customer policy. Deletion APIs available; for Private deployments deletion can be executed by customer ops.

SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness checklist for Sales to collect pre-procurement: (these map to the evidence package we provide)
- Latest SOC2 Type II report (NDA for full report)
- ISO27001 scope statement & certificate (if applicable) or roadmap to certification
- HIPAA BAA template and evidence of operational controls for PHI handling
- Penetration test summary and remediation tracker
- Architecture diagram showing tenancy model and network boundaries
- Data flow diagram showing where logs and payloads traverse and are stored
- Encryption key management details (KMS, customer vs. Redwood)
- Audit log schema sample and example export (CSV/JSON)

Competitive differentiation (how to position vs. cloud providers & self-hosted infra vendors):
- Vs major cloud ML endpoints: "Cloud providers provide primitives; Redwood provides opinionated inference runtime + routing + cost controls out of the box. We expose audit logs, token-level cost attribution, and rollout controls that require expensive glue code on cloud primitives."
- Vs inference self-hosted vendors: "Self-hosting buys control but not the operational playbook. Redwood bundles the serving runtime optimizations (batching, KV caching, quantized kernels) with observability and a catalog of production‑validated model variants so customers avoid long performance tuning cycles."
- Unique: "Unified offering across Hosted, Dedicated, Private means buyers can start fast with Hosted and migrate to Dedicated/Private with configuration and contract continuity (same API, same rollout tooling)."

Attachments & small technical appendix (for RFPs):
- SAMPLE: Audit log JSON schema (short snippet) — include in RFP attachment.
- SAMPLE: SOC2 scope list (control domains included).
- SAMPLE: HIPAA handling checklist for onboarding.

Sample short email for procurement (paste-ready):
Hi [Name],

Thanks for the RFP. Attached is a short evidence package describing Redwood Inference's security controls and data handling commitments. Highlights: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II attestation for our hosted control plane, supports Dedicated and Private deployment models for enhanced isolation, and offers a HIPAA BAA where required. We can provide the SOC2 report and pen test summary under NDA and have a standard BAA template we share during contract negotiations.

Please let me know the evidence items you need and I’ll route them immediately.

Next steps for GTM (recommended):
- Produce a 1-pager "Security at a glance" for sales decks (one-page summary with one-liners + evidence checklist).
- Create a single Confluence evidence page that maps each buyer ask to the artifact we provide (SOC2, architecture diagrams, BAA, pen test).
- Build a "security micro-FAQ" in the onboarding playbook for Solutions Engineers with canned scripts and links to artifacts.
- Create a short demo for Solutions Engineering showing Redwood Console audit log export into Splunk/ELK and token-cost breakdown.

Open questions for product/security alignment (items for the internal queue):
- Standardize default audit-log retention and opt-in for payloads (recommendation: default 30 days, configurable up to 3 years).
- Finalize BAA template and identify legal owner for HIPAA customers.
- Define the minimal Dedicated evidence package (what to provide in lieu of hosted SOC2 report).

Notes / rough ideas (internal, exploratory):
- Consider a "security maturity" badge (bronze/silver/gold) that maps to deployment mode + available artifacts to speed procurement conversations.
- Create a short security video walkthrough that shows how to configure audit exports and KMS integration in Redwood Console.

Document history: v0.1 initial draft (Avery Chen) 2024-10-18; v0.2 added engineering scripts and audit clause (Priya Kapoor) 2024-11-05; v0.3 appended HIPAA BAA notes and procurement email (Mateo Ruiz) 2025-02-09.
